title: feat: support 100 MiB inline-image chat requests
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Accepts chat JSON up to 100 MiB with inline images through the existing API; the media service stores large images before the request reaches the generation coordinator.
- Reuses account-scoped image IDs, so later turns referencing the same image skip the media upload.
- Uses the rewritten request body directly for caching and deduplication, removing the extra raw-body digest and Hono request overrides.
- Keeps the existing 32 MiB path for smaller requests and random media IDs by default.
- Tests 96 MiB parsing and full-route repeated-image behavior, provider URLs, response caching, and the 100 MiB rejection. Gen staging deploy of commit 71fbaa9ec4 succeeded. Two authenticated 33.13 MiB chat turns returned 200; media metadata confirmed the second turn did not re-upload the image.

Addresses #15889. Related: #16020.

gist.headline: A bigger picture fits
gist.blurb: Chat makes room for hefty inline images—up to 100 MiB of JSON. Bring the same image back in a later turn, and the media service remembers it.
gist.summary: The chat API accepts JSON requests up to 100 MiB by storing large inline images in the media service before generation, reusing account-scoped image IDs across turns while retaining the existing 32 MiB path for smaller requests.
gist.impact: Developers can send larger inline-image chats, and repeated references to the same image avoid another media upload while remaining eligible for response caching.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy chat terminal represents the existing API; a media shelf holds a large image parcel labeled 100 MiB, while a return arrow shows the same parcel being referenced on a later turn without carrying it again. Polli delivers the parcel with a tiny messenger satchel, and a CRT monitor robot welcomes it beside code-plants.
